metadata.name: split
metadata.description: Split a file into smaller files

installation.note: split is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: The split command breaks a file into multiple smaller output files. It's useful for chunking large logs, transferring big files in pieces, or preparing data for parallel processing.
when_to_use: Split a large file into smaller chunks for transfer or storage
Break a log file into manageable pieces
Create evenly sized chunks for parallel processing

syntax.description: If INPUT is omitted, split reads from standard input. Output files are named using PREFIX (default: x) with alphabetical suffixes.

options.description: Split by size in bytes (supports suffixes like K, M, G)
options.use_case: When you want chunks of a specific size

options.description: Split by number of lines per output file
options.use_case: When splitting text files by line count

options.description: Use numeric suffixes instead of alphabetic
options.use_case: When you want chunk_00, chunk_01, ... naming

examples.title: Split a file into 100MB chunks
examples.use_case: Transfer or store large files in smaller pieces

examples.title: Split a log file into 1000-line parts
examples.description: Create access_aa, access_ab, ... each with 1000 lines (except the last)

related_commands.description: Recombine split parts by concatenating them in order (e.g., cat chunk_* > original)
Archive files before splitting if you need a single stream
